# std::scope_exit

Module file: `stdlib/std/scope_exit.mla`

`ScopeExit<Action>` is a C++23-inspired scope guard. It owns a zero-argument
action and invokes it automatically when the guard leaves scope, including
when a function returns early. Call `release()` to cancel the action.

```rust
mod std::scope_exit;
use std::scope_exit::scope_exit;

fn write_record() -> i32 {
    let cleanup = scope_exit(|| { println!("record complete"); });
    if !write_header() { return -1; }
    return write_body();
}
```

### API

- `scope_exit(action)` creates an active guard for a zero-argument closure.
- `guard.release()` disables the action without destroying the guard early.
- `guard.is_active()` reports whether cleanup remains armed.

The guard uses Mlang's existing deterministic `free` cleanup hook. Its action
runs once on ordinary scope exit or early return unless `release()` was called.
